title: PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619) — fixed in 8.4.27
note: Description only: names the functions the story touches and how far to walk the call graph. No exploit steps. Colours mark the fixed version's parts: problem=where the bug lived, path=how it was reached, fix=what the patch added or hardened.

incident.title: State corruption via an out-of-memory bailout
incident.summary: When PHP ran out of memory it jumped straight out with a longjmp, leaving half-finished request state behind. A large multipart upload with session upload-progress could reach that state before a request was fully set up. The fix replaces the jump with an orderly unwind and resets the globals that startup touches. This model is the fixed version, 8.4.27.

notes.rfc1867_post_handler: Parses a multipart/form-data body. A big upload here is what drives memory high while a request is still starting up.
notes._emalloc: The request allocator. On out-of-memory it used to bail out with a longjmp instead of returning.
notes._zend_bailout: The longjmp itself: it unwinds the C stack to a landing pad, skipping the cleanup in between. That is what left state half-finished.
notes.php_session_rfc1867_callback: The session upload-progress hook. It runs during body parsing, before the request is fully active, which is why reaching it in a bad state mattered.
notes.php_session_rfc1867_update: Writes upload progress into the session mid-parse. Now guarded so it cannot run user code while the request is not ready.
notes.php_session_rfc1867_cleanup: Removes the progress entry when the upload ends. Guarded the same way.
notes.ps_decode_php_serialize: Decodes the stored session. During upload progress it now decodes in a restricted mode that builds no live objects.
notes.ps_decode_php: The default session decoder, restricted the same way during upload progress.
notes.sapi_handle_post: Hands the POST body to its handler. After the fix it checks for a pending out-of-memory and unwinds cleanly instead of leaving it.
notes.php_session_initialize: Opens and reads the session. The fix lets it fail cleanly and the caller abort, rather than assuming it always succeeds.
notes.zend_handle_delayed_oom: Added by the fix: instead of jumping out on out-of-memory, PHP records it and handles it here at a safe point.
notes.php_request_shutdown: Resets the globals that a request touches, so the next request cannot see state left over from a failed one.

tour.title: php-src
tour.text: This is not all of PHP. It is a slice: a few files on one path, pulled out of almost six thousand functions, with their immediate neighbours. Each planet is a source file, each gate is a function. The bright planets are the core of the story; the dim ring around them is context.

tour.title: rfc1867.c
tour.text: The story starts here, in the code that reads a file upload. A request that uploads a large body makes PHP allocate a lot of memory while the request is still being set up.

tour.title: zend alloc dot c
tour.text: Every allocation goes through the request allocator. The question is what it does when memory runs out.

tour.title: ⚠ the bailout
tour.text: In the old behaviour it bailed out: a longjmp that unwinds the C stack straight to a landing pad, skipping every cleanup step in between. The planets blinking red are where that left things in a bad state.

tour.title: ⚠ session.c
tour.text: The amber path runs through the session. While the upload is still being parsed, the upload-progress hook reads and writes the session, before the request is fully active. On a half-finished request, that was unsafe.

tour.title: ⚠ decoding the session
tour.text: Decoding the stored session could build objects and run their code. Doing that this early, on corrupted state, was the dangerous part.

tour.title: ✓ delayed out-of-memory
tour.sub: zend alloc dot c · the fix
tour.text: Here is the heart of the fix. Instead of jumping out when memory runs low, PHP now records that it happened and handles it later, at a point where the request state is whole. No more jump through half-finished code.

tour.title: ✓ fail cleanly
tour.text: The session code now decodes in a restricted mode during upload progress, builds no live objects, and is allowed to fail so the caller can stop. The green gates are the guard the fix added.

tour.title: ✓ reset between requests
tour.text: And shutdown now resets the globals a request touches, so whatever one request left behind cannot leak into the next.

tour.title: PHP2Shell
tour.text: So the fix was structural. Stop jumping out of a request on out-of-memory, handle it at a safe point, and reset the state in between. The slice shows only the path that mattered, not the whole engine.
